comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C37-C48 regarding the fly model establishment and humanization system. Both evaluations find the genetic rescue experiments, orthology analysis, and functional conservation convincingly demonstrated. All three peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings as 'convincing' and 'well-executed,' matching OpenEval's assessment of methodological soundness.

Agreement on claims C49-C59 regarding Uba5 expression characterization and tissue-specific rescue. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes speculation about neuronal activity (C54), while peer reviewers accept the expression data without specific concerns, noting the 'extensive phenotypic characterization.'

Strong agreement on claims C60-C72 regarding phenotypic classification into three groups. Both evaluations find the classification system convincing with appropriate statistical analyses. All peer reviewers explicitly affirm the 'mild, intermediate, and severe classes' with 'convincing evidence,' matching OpenEval's positive assessment of the comprehensive phenotypic data.

Agreement on claims C73-C89 regarding structural modeling and predictions. Both evaluations support the structural analysis. OpenEval notes that some predictions (C81, C83, C85, C87, C89) are speculative inferences rather than direct experimental evidence. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly states the biochemical effects are 'well predicted by' or 'consistent with' the structural location, accepting the analysis without concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C90-C107 regarding biochemical characterization including thermal stability and ATP-binding assays. Both evaluations find the correlation between biochemical defects and in vivo phenotypes compelling. Peer reviewers note the severity of biochemical defects 'closely track' phenotypic severity, matching OpenEval's assessment of well-controlled experiments with appropriate statistical analyses.

Agreement on claims C108-C118 regarding Group IA variants, particularly p.Ala371Thr. Both evaluations support the temperature-dependent transthiolation defect and correlation with population genetics. Peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge, noting the fly nervous system as a 'powerful model,' consistent with OpenEval's assessment of the compelling biochemical and genetic evidence.

Agreement on claims C119-C126 regarding Group IB variants with intermediate phenotypes. Both evaluations support the correlation between structural location and biochemical defects. OpenEval notes C126 (ER stress speculation) is not directly tested; peer reviewers accept this as appropriately framed hypothesis without challenge, consistent with the overall positive assessment.

Agreement on claims C127-C133 regarding Group III severe loss-of-function variants. Both evaluations support the classification into stability-disrupting versus catalysis-affecting variants. Peer reviewers affirm the 'severe class' with 'convincing evidence,' matching OpenEval's positive assessment of the insolubility data and biochemical characterization.

Agreement on claims C134-C140 regarding genotype-phenotype correlation in human patients. Both evaluations support the correlation analysis. OpenEval notes limited sample size (24 individuals, 17 families) and potential confounding in one case, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the correlation as 'striking' and 'convincing' without raising these specific concerns. Peer R9 also includes C4 which OpenEval addresses separately in R13.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C36 regarding the new clinical case report with p.Gln312Leu variant. Both evaluations support the clinical phenotyping, genetic data from trio exome sequencing, and bioinformatic predictions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the new case by noting it 'provides a basis for evaluating current and future individuals,' matching OpenEval's assessment of valid contribution to literature.

Agreement on claims C141-C146 regarding discussion of related UFMylation pathway disorders and future applications. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes C145-C146 are speculative about future work rather than demonstrated results; peer reviewers accept these as appropriately framed without challenge, with Reviewer 1 affirming the model's utility for future characterization.

Agreement on claims C1-C10, C22 (clinical characterization of DEE44) which overlap with peer R11's broader coverage of background claims C1-C23. Both evaluations support the clinical and mechanistic background as well-cited and established. Peer reviewers accept the disease context and background without challenge, affirming the need to assess disease-associated variants.

Agreement on claims C11-C21 (UFMylation pathway mechanism) which overlap with peer R11's coverage of background claims. Both evaluations support the mechanistic description as well-cited and based on established literature. Peer reviewers accept the background information without challenge, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of extensive citations to biochemical and structural studies.

Agreement on the central finding (C4, C105, C106) regarding correlation between fly phenotypes and biochemical activity. OpenEval R13 addresses this as the manuscript's central contribution with comprehensive supporting data. Peer R9 explicitly affirms this correlation as 'striking' with all three reviewers confirming the finding. Both evaluations view this as a significant advance, though peer R9 covers broader genotype-phenotype claims (C134-C140) while OpenEval R13 focuses specifically on the methodological correlation.
